packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-02 - first reader response (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or a prior reading. The only identifying text seen is the modern pencil shelf labels written on the fragments themselves ("Stams, StA, Frg. 171_1r", "..._2v", "..._3v"), visible in the overview. I did nothing beyond the reader rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg)
- Paper (not parchment, by appearance: soft, stained, water/foxing stains), photographed on black with a ruler and colour chart. Three pieces laid side by side:
  (a) left, a larger leaf, roughly 16 x 30 cm, labelled in modern pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 171_1r"; a strip of modern tape (transparent, shiny) runs horizontally across it about one third down;
  (b) middle, a narrow strip (about 7 cm wide), labelled "Stams, StA, Frg. 171_2v", also with a horizontal tape band at the same height; it looks like the right-hand part of a leaf whose left text is cut off;
  (c) right, a very narrow slip labelled "Stams, StA, Frg. 171_3v" with almost no visible writing, and a tiny separate scrap below it.
- Script: a German cursive (Kurrent-type) documentary hand in brown ink, single column, unruled. Not a book hand.
- Text structure (observation): a list of short entries, each beginning with an enlarged/looped "An dem tag ..." or "Am ..." at the left, followed by 1-3 indented continuation lines, often ending with a count formula like "2 mal geben/gebrn". Marginal numerals stand to the left of some entries on piece (a) ("19"? at top, "5" lower) and to the left of the entries on the far left of the visible text of the right column of (a) ("19", "20", "21", "22"). Tentative interpretation: a register/account of payments or donations, with day numbers in the margin.
- On piece (a), at the right edge there are entry-beginnings ("An...", "Am...") of a second block of text, partly cut by the trimmed edge - perhaps the left edge of the text of the neighbouring column/page, with numerals 19-22 beside them. Tentative.
- No rubrics or decorated initials visible; no interlinear glosses noted at overview scale.
- Overview is reduced; the tiles image-002..010 should be native-resolution tiles of this face (3 x 3 grid by sizes).


TRANSCRIPTION CONVENTIONS: physical lines kept; line numbers counted from top of each image; (..) = proposed expansion; "?" after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = not read. Brown stain is heavy on the upper part of piece (a).

=== image-002.jpg (piece a, top-left tile; text runs off right edge; bottom edge is tape band) ===
002.1  [margin: "-9" or "19"?]  An dem tag pfarr[er?] ...            (runs off right)
002.2      Er?lpffs? · 2 · mal [g...]
002.3  An dem tag Junck? / Jung? ...
002.4      Amner? / Aniner? Martin ge[...]
002.5      Hanns? von Hölblin? / Hölbhn? ...
002.6      ziu? / zwi? mal geben?   [reading "zwi mal gebm" uncertain]
002.7  Der pflegsteurich? / pflagsteinichs? ...  [long word, uncertain]
002.8      ainen? / aimn? geben?
002.9  [margin: "2" partly under tape, likely "20"]  An dem tag ein pfrund? / preng? ...
Note: lines 002.1-002.8 are a single overlapping group of 3 entries; I read the opening formula "An dem tag" confidently (initial A is a large looped form; "dem" is written "dem"/"dē" with minims; "tag" ends in a long-tailed g that resembles "tug").

=== image-003.jpg (piece a, top-right tile; overlaps image-002 on its left; shows a second text block cut at the right edge of piece a) ===
Left text block (continuations of image-002 lines; line numbers here are this tile's own count):
003.1  ...g? pfarrer von          [= end of 002.1: "An dem tag pfarrer von"]
003.2  ...mal geben               [= 002.2, "· 2 · mal geben"]
003.3  ...Junch? / Jung? gerimi? / geriom?   [second word uncertain]
003.4  ...rtin gend? / vnd? her   [= 002.4 "Martin ... her"]
003.5  ...ölblin? jerlichen       [= 002.5 "Hanns? von Hölblin? jerlichen"]
003.6  ...m                       [= 002.6 end "geben"]
003.7  ...münckh? / münch? · 8 · mass?   [= 002.7, "... · 8 · mass"]
003.9  ...in pfrund? / preng? von  [= 002.9 "An dem tag ein ... von"]

Left block line-ends (aligned to 005 lines):

=== SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS ===
- Document type (observation only): German documentary cursive list; entries open "An dem tag ..." with numerals 1-28 (approx.) in the margin; counted formulae "· 2 · mal geben", "ain mal geben", "maß wein", "Zinßleut[e]", "jerlichen". Several personal names / epithets (pfarrer von ..., Hanns ..., pauli/paule Zorn, Jacob Schnider?, Jacob Keller?, Conrad ..., "der Schmid"?) and places ("von Zirl?", "von Rattinberg?", "Siechhauß?", "Petersperg?"). These are image readings only, many uncertain.
- Pieces a and b carry closely parallel formulae on both faces; I could not determine whether b is a second copy, a neighbouring page, or a stub of the same bifolium.
- Areas read: piece a both faces, all lines of the main block (face 1 ~29 lines; face 2 ~32 lines), plus line-ends of a cut-away block on face 2 and line-starts of a second block on face 1. Piece b both faces (line-ends on face 1, line-starts on face 2). Piece c both faces (only 1-2 letters per line).
- Unread/poorly read: lines under the tape band (one line per face on a and b); the stained centre of face-2 entry 24; the end of face-2 entry 28 under the photographic grey mask; most of the second block letters on face 1 (only initials survive). Many proper names are uncertain; letters e/c/r and minim groups are hard to separate in this hand.
- No crops were made (rscratch/packet-02/ was created but left empty). I did not stop on the image limit; all 24 images were read.
